issue.body:
Follow-up to #3432 (in-slicc C toolchain; research note #3402).

## Summary

These are the slicc interop bugs that real C projects hit when they build inside slicc. With them, zlib and Lua build end to end in slicc.

Before, `./configure` came out non-executable after `tar xzf` ("Permission denied"). `$CC -c x.c` with `CC="emcc -O2"` failed with "command not found". The test binaries emcc produced couldn't be run, because slicc parsed them as bash.

Now:

- **zlib 1.3.1:** `tar xzf` → `emconfigure ./configure --static` (33 s) → `emmake make` (63 s) → `make test` prints `*** zlib test OK ***` and `*** zlib 64-bit test OK ***`.
- **Lua 5.4.7:** `make generic CC=emcc …` (recursive Makefile, 93 s) → `./src/lua -e 'print(_VERSION, 6*7)'` prints `Lua 5.4  42`.

## Why

The goal is a C/C++ toolchain that runs inside slicc, so slicc can rebuild the wasm tools it ships. The proof target is ImageMagick, reached through a ladder: zlib → Lua → sqlite → C++ → ImageMagick. Each rung surfaced shell or realm behavior that differs from a POSIX system. Every fix below comes from a failure in one of those builds.

`make` itself is GNU make 4.4.1 built for wasm on the toolchain side, outside this repo.

## Approach / Implementation notes

**Shell**
- **`tar` keeps file and directory modes** (`tar-command.ts`, `ipk/tar.ts`). Create records modes and extract applies them. The default (0644 file / 0755 directory) is skipped for new paths but applied when overwriting. Directory modes are applied after the tree is written, deepest first. A `chmod` the backend can't do (a mount answers ENOSYS) is skipped, so extraction into a mount finishes. `writeTar` defaults to 0644 / 0755 instead of nanotar's group-writable 664 / 775.
- **`tar xzf`** (the traditional dashless form) works like `tar -xzf`.
- **The command word is word-split** (just-bash patch). Upstream expanded the name as one string, so `$CC -c x.c` looked for a command named `emcc -O2`. The first field now runs and the rest become arguments. A quoted `"$X"` stays whole, and an empty expansion falls through to the next word, as in bash.
- **A non-shell shebang runs its interpreter** (just-bash patch). An executable run by path always went through bash with its `#!` dropped, so `./example` built by `emcc -o example` (`#!/usr/bin/env node`) failed to parse. Such a file now runs as `<shebang line> "$0" "$@"`. Shell shebangs (`sh`, `bash`, `dash`, `ash`, `ksh`, `zsh`), files without a shebang, and `bash file` all keep the bash path.
- **`expr STRING : REGEX` takes a POSIX basic regex** (just-bash patch). `\(…\)` groups return the capture, and bare `( ) { } + ? |` are literals. Upstream passed the pattern to `RegExp` as-is, so every autoconf configure died on `expr "x$ac_option" : 'x\([^=]*\)='` ("invalid variable name: 0").
- **`case` / `[[ == ]]` patterns support POSIX bracket expressions** (just-bash patch): `[!…]` negation, a leading `]`, and `[[:alpha:]]`-style classes. Autoconf's `*[!_$as_cr_alnum]*` check rejected every `VAR=value` argument. Filename globs and `${x#…}` were already right.
- **`ls -l` shows the real mode** (just-bash patch) instead of a hardcoded `-rw-r--r--` / `drwxr-xr-x`.
- **`/bin` is the merged-`/usr` alias of the virtual `/usr/bin`** (`vfs-adapter.ts`). `/bin/sh` is where make, `SHELL=/bin/sh` and `posix_spawn` callers look. Other `/bin/*` paths still go to the VFS.

**Python / Node realms**
- **`python3` skips no-op interpreter flags** (`-E -s -S -u -B -I -P -q -O -b -d -R`, bundles like `-Es`, and `-W` / `-X` with their argument). Emscripten's `emcc` launcher runs `python3 -E emcc.py`.
- **`fs.readSync` / `fs.writeSync` work on the standard streams** (`realm-fs-stdio-fd.ts`). fd 0 walks the buffered stdin with a cursor, and fd 1 and 2 go to the sinks. `process.stdin.fd` / `stdout.fd` / `stderr.fd` are 0 / 1 / 2, because Emscripten programs read their terminal with `fs.readSync(process.stdin.fd, …)`. Other fds still throw `EBADF`: there is no fd table.

The five just-bash hunks are recorded in `patches/patches.json` (reason, removeWhen, verify). Each has an upstream issue, linked from `upstream` and from its `removeWhen`:

| Hunk | Upstream issue |
| --- | --- |
| positionals past `$9` (already on `main` via #3432) | vercel-labs/just-bash#456 |
| command-word splitting | vercel-labs/just-bash#457 |
| non-shell shebang dispatch | vercel-labs/just-bash#458 |
| `ls -l` real modes | vercel-labs/just-bash#459 |
| `expr` BRE | vercel-labs/just-bash#460 |
| `case` / `[[ == ]]` `[!…]` negation | vercel-labs/just-bash#461 |

All six still reproduce on the latest just-bash release (3.4.2).

## Cross-cutting impact

- **Floats:** all of them. The shell and the realms are shared.
- **Shell word splitting:** only unquoted expansions in *command* position change behavior. Argument splitting was already correct and is untouched.
- **Shebang dispatch** applies only to scripts run by path. `source`, `bash file` and `sh -c` are unchanged.
- **Archive modes:** ipk's `readTar` entries now carry a `mode`. ipk doesn't use the field, so package installs are unaffected.
- **`/bin`:** `exists` / `stat` / `readdir` of `/bin` and `/bin/<command>` now succeed, where they used to be ENOENT.
- **Bundle size:** the webapp total-JS `size-limit` becomes **27 MiB** (28.31 MB). It had been raised by a few kB in nearly every PR and conflicted on almost every rebase. It now measures 25.92 MB. The first-load delta gate and its eager ceilings still guard the boot graphs: page +0.0 kB, worker +1.0 kB for this PR.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run verify` (8/8) and the boy-scout gate
- [x] `npm run typecheck`
- [x] Full vitest: 24,374 passed. Two `check-touched-exemptions.test.mjs` cases timed out under the full-suite load and pass alone (8/8); that file is unrelated to this PR.
- [x] `npm run test:coverage:webapp`
- [x] `npm run build -w @slicc/webapp` and `npm run build -w @slicc/chrome-extension`, then `npm run bundle-size`
- [x] **New / changed behavior is covered by unit tests**: `tar-command`, `ipk/tar`, `python-command`, `realm-fs-stdio-fd`, `vfs-adapter`, `almost-bash-shell` (`/bin/sh -c`), and one test file per just-bash hunk (`just-bash-command-name-split-patch`, `just-bash-ls-mode-patch`, `just-bash-shebang-patch`, `just-bash-expr-bre-patch`, `just-bash-case-bracket-patch`). The just-bash tests run against both the `node` and `browser` bundles.
- [x] Every new test was checked against the code without its fix. For the just-bash hunks that means a reinstall of pristine just-bash, where they fail.
- [x] Manual smoke (CLI harness built from this branch): the zlib and Lua runs above.

## Documentation

- [x] `docs/` — `docs/node-compat-shims.md`: `readSync` / `writeSync` on stdio and `process.std*.fd`
- [x] `patches/patches.json` — reason / removeWhen / verify for each just-bash hunk

## Risk & rollback

A regression would affect scripts that rely on the old behavior. The likely cases:
- an unquoted multi-word variable used as a command name, which used to fail with "command not found";
- a non-shell `#!` file run by path, which used to run as bash.

Both were bugs relative to bash, so nothing should depend on them. Rolling back means reverting this PR (the patch hunks go with it); nothing is persisted.

## Checklist

- [x] Commits are focused and package-local where possible
- [x] No hand-edited files under `dist/`
- [x] No secrets in the diff
- [x] Shell-command changes are intentional and documented (`patches.json`, `docs/node-compat-shims.md`)
